query: What goal-management practices support high achievement?

per_column.name: primary_intervention_type
per_column.rationale: The type of intervention/action taken is a constitutive aspect of a goal-management practice -- it describes WHAT the practice is, an aspect of the success-factor concept.

per_column.name: automation_lever
per_column.rationale: This is a boolean redundant with primary_intervention_type ('automation' value) and multi_lever_goal; it re-expresses whether the intervention involves automation rather than adding a distinct facet.

per_column.name: feedback_loop_included
per_column.rationale: Presence of a feedback/monitoring loop is a genuine constitutive aspect of a goal-management practice, though it overlaps with the feedback_survey value of intervention_type.

per_column.name: action_specificity
per_column.rationale: How specific the goal action is (specificity of the target) is a real aspect OF goal-management quality -- part of the concept.

per_column.name: benchmark_reference
per_column.rationale: The reference/benchmark against which the goal is set is a constitutive aspect of how the goal is framed and measured.

per_column.name: multi_lever_goal
per_column.rationale: Boolean derived directly from intervention_type/automation_lever (whether more than one lever is used); overlaps with intervention facet rather than carving a new aspect.

per_column.name: measurement_mechanism
per_column.rationale: How progress is measured is a core constitutive aspect of goal management; however it overlaps heavily with benchmark_reference (both concern measurement).

per_column.name: time_horizon
per_column.rationale: The temporal scope of the goal is a distinct constitutive facet of a goal-management practice.

per_column.name: scope_breadth
per_column.rationale: The organizational breadth/scope of the goal is a distinct constitutive facet of the practice.

judge.rationale: Most columns are genuine facets -- aspects OF a goal-management practice (intervention type, specificity, benchmark, measurement, time horizon, scope), satisfying the meronymy claim. However mutual exclusivity is weakened by substantial overlap: automation_lever and multi_lever_goal are derivable restatements of primary_intervention_type, feedback_loop_included duplicates the feedback value of intervention_type, and benchmark_reference overlaps measurement_mechanism (both the measurement facet). Exhaustiveness is fair: the set covers action type, specificity, measurement, benchmarking, timing, and scope, but omits aspects such as ownership/accountability, resourcing, and goal-difficulty/target-setting, and clusters redundantly around a few aspects rather than evenly carving the concept.
